book.ninjacatskies.whisker_codex.pack.en: **Swarm.** There are no bees to find in the void, so you make somewhere a bee wants to be: a ring of oak logs around a small flower, placed on the pad and woken with another flower (right-click it). Wait. Wings.

**Goal:** finish Swarm and seat the Swarm token.\
You need a nest the pad can actually grow — oak logs around a flower, woken with a right-click from another flower — then hives.\
**Check:** Finish Swarm. Claim the token and seat it. The Swarm notch lights.

The Gate Drum is the portable way into the March. Use it empty-handed and play the Gate Rite: hit the falling beats on A, S, D, F. Land 60%% and it opens; no Pulse needed. Do not strike it like a Drumheart.\
Bind a return compass before you go. `/tribalpower gate list` names later gates.

3\. Slot faces, Shatter-on-Kiln, relays, compass landings, ranked machines, Spirit Charms, Pulse lamps and the sixth Loom voice live in that book, not here.\
A held redstone signal pauses generators other than the Drumheart.

**Goal:** find a wild pad-runner in the March, not on your void pad.\
You need a **Gate Drum**, **Gysahl**, and the **Chocobo Almanac**.\
Birds do not spawn on a skyblock island. There is no spawn-egg shortcut and no join gift. Walk the March.

1\. Use a **Gate Drum** empty-handed and play the Gate Rite (hit the beats on A, S, D, F; 60%% opens it), then walk through. Yellows graze the Steppe and Reed Fen. Snow Fields hide Wonderful grades. Ember Wastes keep Flame birds.

2\. Pick **Gysahl** in the March (Reed Fen is densest). Picking drops seeds too; plant them on farmland at home.\
3\. Craft the **Chocobo Almanac** (book and a gysahl leaf) and use it anywhere: its pages list your own birds.

After you have walked the March, **Esther** stands at Clowder Hall (`/clowder hub`). Ride a saddled bird to her, ask the Whiskerwind Guide, or craft a **Chocobo Pocketwatch** (gold nuggets around a clock, with a gysahl).\
**Check:** you are on a saddled bird, or Esther is waiting at the hub.

**Goal:** train, mate, and paint colours without chasing dyes that do not exist.\
You need greens to train, nuts to mate, and the **Chocobo Almanac** to read the bird.

1\. Train an adult on greens until it is sated on each kind. Gysahl is the only green in the wild; Krakka is two gysahl and bone meal.\
2\. Mate with nuts. Talent follows the nut. Colour follows the parents unless Carob or Zeio is involved.
3\. **Carob** (Bilo at Whiskerwind, or Class A races): two Good-or-better Yellows hatch Green or Blue. Each parent needs 1 first-place race; 4 combined firsts make the colour certain.
4\. Green plus Blue hatch Black (a miss is White) — 2 firsts each, 9 combined for a sure roll. **Zeio** (Bilo, rare at Class S): Black plus a Wonderful Yellow hatch Gold — 3 firsts each, 12 combined.

5\. There are no Pink or Red birds. The Fair stall does not sell those dyes. Purple is End; Flame is Ember Wastes; Gold flies.\
**Check:** the Almanac shows colour, grade, class, race wins and the last nut. Recipes stay in JEI.

The old world
What hung, what fell, what fixing means.
What the world was

Before the void had a name, the sky was a floor. Nine Strands of living thread — Soil, Stone, Sprout, Claw, Spark, Clock, Swarm, Sigil, Spindle — were pulled taut by nine tribes of Ninjacats. Continents hung from that lattice the way fruit hangs from a well-kept vine.

Cities did not float. They hung, and hanging felt like standing. Weather ran on a schedule, not a mood. Rain knew where to fall. Nothing dropped that was not meant to. The old world was not peace. It was maintenance.
How it fell

Something severed the Loom. The Codex does not know what. Maintenance stopped. Eight pulls became eight arguments about whose fault the slack was. The Spindle seam tore. Continents fell. Weather forgot its roads. The tribes scattered with whatever dirt they could carry.

What did not fall is what you are standing on: pads of earth the Strands still remember. Factories kept running. Drums kept beating. Gates stood open into nowhere. The March caught the wreckage — a grave and a harbour at once.
What fixing means

You are not rebuilding the hanging continents. You are teaching nine Strands to agree again, one pad at a time. A seated token is a promise kept. A Clowder that seats the Fragment closes its Strand of the Fray. When every Clowder has done the same, the column over the Dock turns to lit thread.
The world does not snap back. It learns to hold. Honest hammocks last longer than floors that lie.
The Old Sky chapter

**The Old Sky** is the rest of this story, written as the tribes would tell it. It does not open all at once. As each Strand seats, that tribe's memory unlocks: hearths, meshes, roots, footholds, drums, songs, hives, seals, gates.
Come back to that chapter when a token is seated. They only talk once you have kept their promise. This page is the always-open version — enough to start the work without waiting for the record.

Tokens and the Post
How a Strand actually counts.

Right-click a Tribe Hearth with what its tribe favours, or with a charged Pulse Cell, and your standing rises: Guest at 50, Friend at 150, Kin at 400, Voice at 800.\
Kills near the hearth and completed trades count.\
Hurting Kin costs 25 and turns the Hunters on you.

Breaking a tribe banner costs five, the hearth forty.\
Generic camp blocks do not cost.

Their hearth favours March Crystal, Loom Thread, compasses. Their Elder trades Loom Thread and a Waystone Compass at Friend, a Loom Anchor and a Loom Seal at Kin, and at Voice standing presses the tribe's Mark into your hand.
